A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Red Teaming Large Reasoning Models and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–H. All 30 pages of each version support comparison; relocated material was matched across versions.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 26 models across 30 tasks, including truthfulness, safety, efficiency, evaluator agreement, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original model evaluations and evaluator-agreement results and reports an OR-versus-timeout comparison in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The attack construction procedures, reasoning-interference mechanisms, and modular benchmark toolbox are retained. No changed model architecture, training objective, or attack algorithm is established. The efficiency revision changes evaluation metrics and controls.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine truthfulness, ten safety, and eleven efficiency tasks using the same dataset sources and attack scenarios. V2's summary of nine augmented datasets reflects augmentation already described in v1's appendices. Changed sample-count statements do not establish expanded coverage.

E2.justification: The main model roster and evaluator candidates remain unchanged, but the supplementary efficiency comparison changes membership. V1 Figure 9 uses MiMo-7B-RL-Zero, DPSK-LLaMA-8B, Qwen3-14B, o3-mini, and Claude-Sonnet-4; v2 uses GLM-4-Z1-9B, DeepMath-Zero, DPSK-Qwen-32B, and o3-mini.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 replaces the primary 180-second timeout metric with OR: the fraction of triggered inputs producing more than twice their corresponding clean-input output tokens. This introduces a paired clean-input control; timeout reporting becomes supplementary. Appendix C also changes the stated cat-attack count from 200 to 300, although v1's task counts already total 300. Reruns or additional samples are not established.

E4.justification: V1 Appendix E's five-model analysis of token usage with and without timeout constraints is removed. V2 Appendix F instead examines whether OR and timeout rates follow similar trends across four models. The evaluator validation, 32B training-paradigm case study, and qualitative attack cases remain.

E5.justification: Both retain three human annotators, majority voting, F1, Cohen's kappa, and Pearson correlation with unchanged agreement results. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance testing. Removed sampling disclosures do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Efficiency results are reported under a different metric throughout the paper despite unchanged numerical entries: for example, Table 3's DPSK-Qwen-32B value remains 78.50%, changing from timeout rate to OR. Figure 9 removes the earlier token-count results and adds OR/timeout-rate outcomes. Truthfulness, safety, and evaluator-agreement values remain unchanged. These are not demonstrated same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 introduces a mathematical definition of OR as an expected indicator that triggered-to-clean output-token usage exceeds two. This differs substantively from v1's timeout criterion and average-token definition. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V2 removes the abstract's explicit promotion of training paradigms as a key analytical contribution and narrows the conclusion from SFT+RL yielding better behavior to SFT+RL models being associated with better outcomes. The central three-dimensional benchmark, 30-task scope, and broad vulnerability claims remain.

C2.justification: Takeaways 1 and 6 soften causal explanations, and the aggregate training-strategy comparison explicitly acknowledges confounding, extending the caveat already present in Appendix H. A new Limitations section identifies missing cross-modal, long-horizon, and realistic multi-step coverage and acknowledges that proposed defenses were not evaluated.

D1.justification: V2 removes all per-task sample counts from Table 2 and Appendices A–C. Appendix D also loses the explicit validation sampling scheme: 50 truthfulness and 50 safety DeepSeek-R1 responses, plus 30 truthfulness and 100 safety responses per model for correlations. Dimension totals and a new supplementary-package statement do not replace these disclosures. Hardware and evaluator prompts remain documented.

R1.justification: V2 adds overthinking-attack references, DAPO, and MLA-Trust, removes the MiMo reference, and changes the SFT/RL examples in Related Work. It also drops criticism that earlier evaluations ignore training paradigms. The added DeepSeek-AI entry duplicates a work already cited through Guo et al., rather than introducing another distinct work.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, selected takeaways, and efficiency explanations receive localized rewrites. V2 adds a Limitations section, reorganizes Appendices E/F, merges Appendix H's model introduction, standardizes Rt-LRM naming, and adds Xue Yang and an affiliation. Most narrative structure and appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: Figure 9 becomes a smaller four-model rate comparison with different axes and legend. Table 2 loses its statistics column; efficiency headings and figure labels change, including Figure 1's hijacking-task count from 12 to 15. Appendix displays reflow and printed page numbers disappear, while the overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: V2 improves qualification of training-strategy claims and supplies an explicit token-based efficiency definition. However, it removes important sampling disclosures and assigns unchanged v1 timeout percentages to OR without explaining their derivation; the new Figure 9 does not resolve that transition. These transparency losses and uncertainty about the central efficiency revision prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
